narrative_purpose: This figure shows the chapter's core mechanism literally: a single coral polyp housing photosynthetic algae in its tissue, passing sugar inward while secreting a stone cup, so the reader sees how sunlight caught by an alga inside an animal becomes reef rock.
subject: A large cutaway of one coral polyp: a soft translucent sac-shaped animal with a ring of slender tentacles at the top, sitting in a pale cup-shaped stone skeleton it has secreted around its base. The transparent body wall is densely packed with many small round golden-brown algal cells that glow softly. Fine streams of tiny pale sugar-particles flow inward from the algae into the animal's body; near the base, the animal is visibly laying down new pale stone, the skeleton drawn thicker and brighter on the sunlit side than on the shaded side. Overhead, soft parallel shafts of light descend through water into the tentacles.
scene: A close intimate view against dark tropical shallow water, one polyp isolated so its inner workings are readable, faint neighbouring polyps blurred behind.
camera: Head-on cutaway at polyp scale, the animal centred and cross-sectioned so both the algae-filled tissue and the stone cup are visible at once.
